title: The TREM2-APOE pathway drives the transcriptional phenotype of dysfunctional microglia in neurodegenerative diseases

one_line: The TREM2-APOE pathway drives a phenotypic switch in microglia from a homeostatic to a neurodegenerative state following the phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons.
summary: This study identifies a specific APOE-dependent molecular signature in microglia across models of ALS, MS, and AD, as well as in human AD brains. Phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons triggers a switch from a homeostatic state to a neurodegenerative phenotype (MGnD) characterized by the suppression of TGF-beta signaling. This phenotypic shift is mediated by TREM2, which induces APOE signaling. Genetic targeting of the TREM2-APOE pathway restored the homeostatic microglial signature and prevented neuronal loss in acute neurodegeneration models. Furthermore, the APOE-mediated MGnD phenotype was linked to the loss of microglial tolerogenic function, suggesting this pathway as a therapeutic target for restoring homeostatic microglia.

key_claims.claim: The TREM2-APOE pathway mediates a switch from homeostatic to neurodegenerative microglia.
key_claims.evidence: Genetic deletion of Trem2 or Apoe in AD and ALS models restored homeostatic genes (e.g., P2ry12, Tmem119) and suppressed inflammatory molecules.
key_claims.location: Results: Genetic targeting of Trem2 suppresses the APOE pathway and restores the homeostatic microglia in APP-PS1 and SOD1 mice

key_claims.claim: MGnD microglia are associated with neuritic Aβ-plaques.
key_claims.evidence: Clec7a+P2ry12- microglia were found in close proximity to neuritic Aβ-plaques and dystrophic neurites in APP-PS1 mice and human AD tissue.
key_claims.location: Results: The MGnD-microglia subset is associated with neuritic Aβ-plaques and diffuse neuritic dystrophy in the AD cortex

key_claims.claim: Phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons suppresses homeostatic microglia and induces the MGnD phenotype.
key_claims.evidence: Injection of apoptotic neurons into naive mice brain induced Apoe expression and changed microglia morphology, whereas live neurons or PBS did not.
key_claims.location: Results: Phagocytosis of apoptotic neurons suppresses homeostatic microglia

key_claims.claim: APOE activation suppresses microglial tolerogenic function.
key_claims.evidence: Ex vivo assays showed that WT microglia at peak EAE fail to suppress T cell proliferation, whereas Apoe-/- microglia maintain this ability, which is abrogated by adding recombinant Apoe.
key_claims.location: Results: Activation of the APOE pathway suppresses the tolerogenic function of microglia

methods.design: In vivo and in vitro animal models alongside post-mortem human brain tissue analysis
methods.population: Mouse models (SOD1 G93A, APP-PS1, EAE, Apoe-/-, Trem2-/-) and post-mortem human AD and control cortex samples

limitations: Human neuronal apoptosis is a rare event compared to focal apoptosis (synaptosis/necroptosis), which may limit the direct translational relevance of the apoptotic neuron injection model.
The data distribution for statistical analysis was explicitly assumed to be normal without formal testing, which could impact the validity of the statistical significance.
red_flags: Authors state 'Data distribution was assumed to be normal, but this was not formally tested', undermining the rigor of the parametric statistical tests used.
